==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(H)yeh₁-}}
From {{der|en|enm|subget}}, from {{der|en|fro|suget}}, from {{der|en|la|subiectus||lying under or near, adjacent, also subject, exposed}}, as a noun, {{m|la|subiectus||a subject, an inferior}}, {{m|la|subiectum||the subject of a proposition}}, past participle of {{m|la|subiciō||throw, lay, place}}, from {{m|la|sub||under, at the foot of}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw, hurl}}, as a calque of {{der|en|grc|ὑποκείμενον}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|sŭbʹjĕkt}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈsʌb.d͡ʒɛkt/}}
* {{lb|en|also}}  {{IPA|en|/ˈsʌb.d͡ʒɪkt/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-subject-noun.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|sub|ject}}

====Adjective====
{{en-adj}}

# Likely to be [[affected]] by or to [[experience]] something; liable.
#: {{ux|en|a country '''subject''' to extreme heat}}
#: {{ux|en|Menu listings and prices are '''subject''' to change.}}
#: {{ux|en|He's '''subject''' to sneezing fits.}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Mac Flecknoe|passage=All human things are '''subject''' to decay.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time T time]| passage=The ability to shift profits to low-tax countries by locating intellectual property in them{{...}}is often assumed to be the preserve of high-tech companies.{{...}}current tax rules make it easy for all sorts of firms to generate{{...}}“stateless income”: profit '''subject''' to tax in a jurisdiction that is neither the location of the factors of production that generate the income nor where the parent firm is domiciled.}}
# [[conditional|Conditional]] upon something; used with ''to''.
#: {{ux|en|The local board sets local policy, '''subject''' to approval from the State Board.}}
# Placed or situated under; lying below, or in a lower situation.
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|1|11|passage=Long he them bore above the '''subject''' plain}}
# Placed under the power of another; owing allegiance to a particular sovereign or state.
#* {{RQ:Locke Government}}, ''Book I''
#*: Esau was never '''subject''' to Jacob.

===Etymology 2===
From {{der|en|la|subiectus||a subject, an inferior}}, {{m|la|subiectum||the subject of a proposition}}, past participle of {{m|la|subiciō||throw, lay, place}}, from {{m|la|sub||under, at the foot of}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw, hurl}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|sŭbʹjĕkt}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈsʌb.d͡ʒɛkt/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈsʌb.d͡ʒɪkt/|a=RP}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-subject-noun.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|sub|ject}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|n-grammar}} {{lb|en|grammar}} The noun, pronoun or [[noun phrase]] about whom the statement is made. In active clauses with verbs denoting an action, the '''subject''' is the actor. In clauses in the [[passive voice]] the '''subject''' is the ''target'' of the action.
#: {{ant|en|object<id:n-grammar>|;|predicate<id:Q179080>}}
#: {{cot|en|agent<id:grammar>|patient<id:linguistics>|;|rheme<id:linguistics>|theme<id:linguistic counterpart to rheme>}}
#: {{ux|en|In the active sentence ‘The cat ate the mouse’, ‘the cat’ is the '''subject''' and ‘the mouse’ is the object.}}
#: {{ux|en|In the passive sentence ‘the mouse was eaten by the cat’, ‘the mouse’ is the '''subject''' even though it is the target (patient) of the action, and ‘the cat’ is the agent.}}
# By extension: an [[actor]] or [[agent#English:_grammar|agent]]; one who takes action.
#: {{ux|en|the '''subjects''' and objects of power}}
# The main [[topic]] of a paper, work of [[art]], [[discussion]], [[field of study]], etc.
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=8|passage=this '''subject''' for heroic song|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Du Fresnoy Dryden Painting|passage=Make choice of a '''subject''' beautifull and noble, which {{...}} shall {{...}}afford{{...}} an ample field of matter wherein to expatiate itself.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=V|scene=i|passage=I am th' unhappy '''subject''' of these quarrels. All these quarrels are about me.}}
#* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|chapter=The Hocussing of Cigarette|passage=Then I had a good think on the '''subject''' of the hocussing of Cigarette, and I was reluctantly bound to admit that once again the man in the corner had found the only possible solution to the mystery.}}
#* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=5|passage=The departure was not unduly prolonged.{{...}}Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments on the '''subject''' of Divine Intention in the disposition of buckets; farewells and last commiserations; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.}}
# A particular area of study.
#: {{ux|en|Her favorite '''subject''' is physics.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-06-14|volume=411| issue=8891| title=[http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21604091-it-possible-sniff-out-problems-sewer-pipes-they-happen-its-gas It's a gas]| passage=One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains.{{...}}But out of sight is out of mind. And that, together with the inherent yuckiness of the '''subject''', means that many old sewers have been neglected and are in dire need of repair.}}
# A [[citizen]] in a [[monarchy]].
#: {{ux|en|I am a British '''subject'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|author=Parliament of the United Kingdom|title=w:Limitation Act 1980|chapter=Part III, section 37(1)|url=[s:Limitation Act 1980#37.1{{!}}Wikisource]|page=26|text=Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Act, and without prejudice to section 39, this Act shall apply to proceedings by or against the [[Crown]] in like manner as it applies to proceedings between '''subjects'''.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1996
|author=w:S. C. M. Paine
|title=Imperial Rivals: China, Russia, and Their Disputed Frontier
|url=https://archive.org/details/imperialrivalsch00pain/
|publisher=w:M. E. Sharpe
|ISBN=1-56324-724-0
|LCCN=96-10750
|OCLC=832696260
|page=89
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/imperialrivalsch00pain/page/89
|text=Ignat'ev refused to concede these points, but offered other concessions instead: Russia would not demand a consulate in Ch'i-ch'i-ha-erh or Chang-chia-k'ou (Kalgan); it would permit Chinese '''subjects''' to continue living along the Ussuri river as Chinese '''subjects'''; and it would limit to 200 the number of Russian traders in Peking.}}
# A person ruled over by another, especially a monarch or state authority.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|author=Alan Mikhail|title=God's Shadow|isbn=9781631492396|page=93|passage={{...}}the Grand Khan seemed to grasp the "truth" of the religion and might become a convert, thereby gaining for Christianity the souls of all his '''subjects'''.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} The main [[theme]] or [[melody]], especially in a [[fugue]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1878|author=William Smith Rockstro|chapter=Subject|title=A Dictionary of Music and Musicians
|passage=The earliest known form of '''subject''' is the ecclesiastical ''cantus firmus'', or plain song.}}
# {{senseid|en|subject of an experiment}} A human, animal{{,}} or an inanimate object that is being [[examine]]d, [[treat]]ed, [[analyse]]d, etc; especially, one being studied in a scientific [[experiment]], such as a [[clinical trial]].
#: {{hypo|en|participant<id:Q4204239>}}
#: {{coi|en|human '''subject''' research}};   {{coi|en|animal '''subjects'''}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1748|author=w:Conyers Middleton|title=Life of Cicero
|passage=Writers of particular lives{{...}}are apt to be prejudiced in favour of their '''subject'''.}}
# {{lb|en|philosophy}} A [[being]] that has [[subjective]] experiences, subjective [[consciousness]], or a relationship with another entity.
# {{lb|en|logic}} That of which something is stated.
# {{lb|en|math}} A [[variable]] [[isolate]]d on one side of an [[equality]], [[express]]ed [[in terms of]] other variables.
#: {{ux|en|Making <math>x</math> the '''subject''' of <math>x^2 - 6x + 3y = 0</math>, we get <math>x = 3 \pm \sqrt{9 - 3y}</math>.}}

===Etymology 3===
From {{der|en|la-med|subiectō}}, iterative of {{m|la|subiciō||throw, lay, place}}, from {{m|la|sub||under, at the foot of}} + {{m|la|iaciō||throw, hurl}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|səb-jĕktʹ}}, {{IPA|en|/səbˈd͡ʒɛkt/|/sʌbˈd͡ʒɛkt/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-subject-verb.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛkt|s=2}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|construed with '''to'''}} To cause (someone or something) to undergo a particular experience, especially one that is unpleasant or unwanted.
#: {{ux|en|I came here to buy souvenirs, not to be '''subjected''' to a tirade of abuse!}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2026 August 19|author=Richard Wilcock|title=Structure and power in the times of GBR|journal=RAIL||issue=1068|page=21|text=But political tinkering is never far away and British Rail, during much of its life, was '''subjected''' to it.}} 
# {{senseid|en|subdue}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To make [[subordinate]] or [[subservient]]; to [[subdue]] or [[enslave]]; to [[subjugate]].
